title: Growth Paths and Feedback Cadence — Handbook for Managers and ICs
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview

This handbook describes Redwood Inference’s repeatable approach to: (1) connecting hiring decisions to long-term career pathways, (2) onboarding new hires for predictable ramp and engagement, and (3) running a consistent feedback and performance cadence for both individual contributors (ICs) and managers. It is intended for people leaders, hiring managers, and individual contributors who want clarity on expectations, timelines, and templates.

Scope

- Roles: ICs, managers, senior managers, and directors across Eng, Product, Research, and GTM functions.
- Processes covered: interview scorecards, offer/acceptance KPIs, 30/60/90 onboarding milestones, quarterly feedback cycles, promotion readiness checklists, and manager coaching cadence.

Principles

1. Predictable ramp: New hires should reach baseline productivity within a measurable window (target: 8 weeks for ICs; 12 weeks for manager roles).
2. Continuous feedback: Frequent, low-stakes feedback reduces surprises at review time.
3. Transparent career paths: Promotion criteria and leveling rubrics must be written and accessible.
4. Hiring with the future in mind: Interviewers evaluate for current-fit and growth signals aligned to career ladders.

Key Metrics (People Ops KPIs)

- Median time-to-fill (offer accepted): 28 days
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 70%
- New-hire 90-day retention target: >= 92%
- Median ramp-to-baseline productivity (IC): 8 weeks
- Candidate NPS (post-interview survey): >= 40

Hiring: Linking Role Specs to Career Ladders

1) Role spec and leveling alignment
- For every requisition, the hiring manager must attach: role spec, target level (e.g., IC2/IC3/Mgr1), and the excerpt of the relevant career ladder.
- Recruiter and hiring manager jointly confirm 3 core success signals (technical skill, cross-functional impact, and communication) used on the scorecard.

2) Interview loop design
- Standard interview loop for IC3+ engineering hires: phone screen (recruiter), technical whiteboard, system design, teammate-shot (pairing), leadership interview.
- Each interviewer must complete the standardized scorecard within 24 hours of interview.

Interview scorecard (required fields)

- Candidate name (string)
- Role applied (string)
- Level expectation (IC2/IC3/Mgr1)
- Core competency ratings (1–5): technical craft, problem solving, collaboration, ownership, communication
- Growth signal: yes/no + evidence
- Hire / No hire / Hire with conditions (recommendation)
- Short rationale (2–4 sentences)

Debrief and decision timeline

1. Debrief meeting within 48 hours of final loop.
2. Hiring manager synthesizes scorecards and publishes a recommended decision in Greenhouse/ATS within 4 business days of offer approval.

Offer and negotiation guidance

- Compensation offers must be approved by People Ops and Compensation within the role’s band.
- Use the standard offer template (HR template link) and include: start date, manager name, remote policy, first-week schedule, and relocation support if applicable.
- Target acceptance window: 72 hours (extend only with approval from People Ops).

Onboarding: 30/60/90 Milestone Plan

Purpose: A structured plan reduces time-to-impact and improves retention. People Ops provides a templated milestone plan that managers must customize within 48 hours of hire acceptance.

Week 0–1: Orientation and setup
- Tasks for People Ops: send welcome packet, create accounts (OKR tracker, internal wiki, Slack), schedule HR kickoff and benefits overview.
- Manager checklist: schedule 1:1 cadence (weekly for first 8 weeks), arrange team introductions, assign onboarding buddy, deliver first-week goals.

Week 2–4: Foundational knowledge and small wins
- Deliverables: complete 2 small code reviews or feature tickets (for engineers), complete product domain readouts, attend core-system walkthroughs.
- 30-day sync: manager-led check-in focused on clarity of role, blockers, and career aspirations. Template agenda below.

Weeks 5–12: Increasing ownership
- Deliverables: lead a small cross-functional workstream, present a lessons learned doc, demonstrate ownership of at least one recurring operational task.
- 60- and 90-day reviews: documented evaluation against onboarding milestones.

Onboarding buddy program

- Purpose: reduce social friction and provide operational help.
- Buddy responsibilities (first 8 weeks): checklist walkthroughs, informal Q&A, first code review pairing. Buddy assignment made by manager before day 1.

Performance & Feedback Cadence

Engine: ongoing feedback + quarterly formal checkpoints.

1) Weekly 1:1s (manager + direct report)
- Frequency: weekly for first 12 weeks, then at least biweekly.
- Suggested 30-min agenda: quick pulse (5 min), progress on goals (10 min), blockers (5 min), career development item (10 min).

2) Monthly skip-level or upward feedback (optional)
- Managers should solicit upward feedback twice per year as part of development. People Ops runs an anonymized pulse once per quarter.

3) Quarterly performance checkpoints (lightweight)
- Purpose: maintain alignment and surface course corrections before annual reviews.
- Inputs: manager notes, direct-report self-assessment (one paragraph), peer feedback (optional).
- Outcomes: on-track / needs coaching / action plan.

4) Annual review and calibration
- Timeline: performance calibration in November; written review delivered by manager in December.
- Promotion windows are twice per year: end of June and December. Promotion packets require: manager narrative, 3 peer reviewers, and level rubric mapping.

Promotion readiness checklist (manager-owned)

- Demonstrated impact beyond current scope (examples)
- Consistent delivery against objectives for >= 6 months
- Positive peer feedback on collaboration and leadership behaviors
- Clear examples of mentorship or cross-team influence (for IC-to-senior transitions)
- 3rd-party reviewer sign-offs and documented learning plan post-promotion

Manager responsibilities and expectations

- Onboarding: deliver customized 30/60/90 by day 2.
- Feedback: run weekly 1:1s and quarterly checkpoints; document key actions in the people ops system.
- Hiring: build diverse interview panels; ensure scorecards submitted on time; coach interviewers on bias mitigation.
- People development: own and update career ladder examples for your team; run promotion calibration sessions at least annually.

Templates and reproducible artifacts

1) 30-minute new-hire 30-day sync agenda
- 5 min: personal check-in
- 10 min: accomplishments / signals of progress
- 10 min: blockers and support needed
- 5 min: next steps and growth topic to explore

2) Interview debrief template (copy into ATS comment)
- Candidate: [name]
- Role / level: [role] / [level]
- One-line recommendation: [Hire / No hire / Hire with conditions]
- Evidence bullets (max 5): [bullet points]
- Risk areas and mitigation: [bullet points]

3) Promotion packet checklist (manager)
- Manager narrative (1–2 pages)
- 3 peer reviewers + short commentary
- Work samples / PR list / project summary
- Rubric mapping table (level -> evidence)
- Proposed salary band and justification

Coaching and calibration playbook (brief)

- If an IC is rated as Needs Coaching for two consecutive quarters, manager and People Ops co-create a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP-lite):
  1. Define specific, measurable objectives (4–8 weeks)
  2. Assign a coach or mentor and weekly check-ins
  3. Review at 30 and 60 days with clear success criteria
- PIP-lite is intended as development-first; escalate to formal HR action only after documented follow-through.

Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices in hiring

- Require at least one diverse-slate candidate for every open role at manager level and above.
- Interview panels must include at least one interviewer trained in inclusive interviewing practices for leadership hires.
- People Ops provides anonymized candidate-slate reporting by requisition to hiring managers monthly.

Operational integrations and tools

- ATS: Greenhouse (requisition, scorecards, offer letters)
- HRIS: BambooHR (onboarding, benefits enrollment)
- Feedback/tracking: Lattice (1:1 notes, goal tracking, promotion packets)
- Documentation: internal Confluence space (templates and ladders)

Escalation paths

- Hiring delays > 30 days: hiring manager escalates to Recruiting Lead and People Ops partner.
- Offer negotiation impasse: People Ops Lead + Compensation partner mediates.
- Performance concerns impacting team safety: immediate consult with People Ops and Legal.

Appendices

Appendix A — Example 90-day deliverables (engineering IC3)
- Complete three feature PRs with reviews and production rollout notes
- Reduce cycle time on assigned module by 10% via automation or refactor
- Lead a postmortem for one operational incident

Appendix B — Suggested discussion prompts for career conversations
- Where do you want to be in 12 months? 24 months?
- What technical skills would you like to explore?
- Who do you want to mentor or learn from?

Appendix C — Quick links (internal)
- Career ladders: /confluence/people-ops/career-ladders
- Offer templates: /confluence/people-ops/offer-templates
- Onboarding checklist: /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-checklists-2024

If you have questions or need help customizing a promotion packet or onboarding plan, contact People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com or schedule time with Priya Kapoor (People Ops Partner).
